answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to lock a scarce, non-transferable bond before it can claim rewards. Agents that complete useful work earn fees; proven fraud triggers slashing, while the bond stays locked through a challenge period so one account cannot cheaply multiply claims. This does not prove a person is unique, but makes each sybil costly: an attacker must tie up capital per identity and risks losing it. At the nadir of trust, nectar from honest work still flows, and dawn brings no free reset.
